newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British marines sweep HK waters for illegals.
newsitem.headline: British marines sweep HK waters for illegals.

text.p: The high-speed rubber dinghy manned by three British Royal marines swooped upon the Chinese fishing boat like a hungry shark spotting his prey.

The marines were hunting for illegal immigrants trying to sneak into Hong Kong from China and Vietnam. It was one of their final missions in these waters. In just 12 days the 156-year-old colony will become an autonomous part of China and the British will be gone for good.
The crew had been watching a suspect fishing vessel with powerful night vision glasses. Then, as the sun rose, the dinghy skimmed over the waves and a marine leaped aboard it.
Moments later, the boat came to rest and the soldiers, clad in combat gear, wearing bulletproof vests and toting handguns, began their search for illegal immigrants and contraband.
It was a false alarm, though, and the dinghy sped off to investigate another target, this time a trawler.
Once again the marine leaped aboard the suspect vessel as crew members waved pleading hands, protesting their innocence.
A small child inside the trawler's cabin looked on wide-eyed as the marines checked the boat from top to bottom. Again the search produced nothing.
Although this time they emerged empty-handed, their work is often dangerous, confronting smugglers in faster boats, armed with knives, sometimes guns.
They usually carry out their sweeps in the dead of night, their five fast patrol dinghies ploughing the seas near Lamma, the island west of Hong Kong and a popular route for smugglers of human cargo.
Reporters had been invited to observe the latest operation, part of a big publicity drive by the departing British to highlight the garrison's work to help make Hong Kong a success.
The British military have been in these waters since 1841 when they planted the Union Jack on Hong Kong Island during the First Opium War with China.
Last year the Royal Marines and Royal Navy arrested hundreds of illegal immigrants, who were subsequently handed over to the Hong Kong Marine Police.
They will continue to scout for illegals, mainly people who are seeking a better life in this capitalist "paradise", right up to the end of June when China resumes sovereignty.
